football_evidence.assessment: No material disagreement: EdgeDesk and the line are within 0.8 points.
supporting: When Florida State has the ball (the line of scrimmage on running plays): Florida State’s offense is stopped at or behind the line on 10.5% of its runs, and Clemson’s defense stops 18.0% of opponent runs at or behind the line (FBS average 17.4%).

When Clemson has the ball (pass protection against the pass rush): Clemson’s offense has allowed a sack on 8.8% of its dropbacks, and Florida State’s defense sacks the quarterback on 8.8% of opponent dropbacks (FBS average 5.7%).

When Florida State has the ball (big plays through the air): Florida State’s offense turns 16.6% of its pass plays into explosive gains, and Clemson’s defense gives up explosive gains on 6.7% of opponent pass plays (FBS average 10.3%).

When Florida State has the ball (big plays on the ground): Florida State’s offense turns 6.1% of its runs into explosive gains, and Clemson’s defense gives up explosive gains on 8.3% of opponent runs (FBS average 6.5%).
